newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels threaten to attack ships in north.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels threaten to attack ships in north.

text.p: Tamil Tiger separatists warned on Tuesday that they would attack ships in the seas off the northern Jaffna peninsula because they carried supplies to the Sri Lankan military.
"Under these conditions, the LTTE has no option but to regard these military-servicing Sri Lankan vessels as legitimate military targets," the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam said in a statement.
The statement, issued from the London office of LTTE, said that, although the Sri Lankan government claimed it was feeding the people of Jaffna, it was really equipping its army in the peninsula.

"We cannot be party to the government ruse of shipping war materials to Jaffna under the pretext of supplying food and necessities for the people," it quoted the LTTE leadership as saying in an official policy statement.

"The LTTE is not prepared to compromise the security of the Tamil people and will, therefore, do its utmost to prevent the traffic of items which do nothing other than strengthen Sri Lanka's military capability," the statement said.
Sri Lanka is forced to transport all supplies to Jaffna by sea or air because there is no road linking the peninsula with the rest of the island.
The Sri Lankan military is in the midst of a huge offensive to open a land route to Jaffna. But the operation has slowed down after two counter-attacks by the rebels last month.
Scores of soldiers and rebels were killed in the fighting.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
The LTTE rebels, who are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east, have attacked two ships in recent weeks.

They attacked and hijacked a North Korean merchant vessel off Point Pedro on the Jaffna peninsula last week. The rebels killed the ship's fourth officer in a shoot-out as they took control of the vessel and abducted its 37 surviving crew.
The crew were released last week.
A week earlier, the rebels torched a refugee ship off the northwestern coast of Mannar and abducted its nine crew members, including two Indonesians who were later released.
A military spokesman told a news conference last week that more attacks were expected on ships ferrying food and other essential supplies to Jaffna.
"They (rebels) will continue doing these kinds of things, hijacking ships and attacking them, but we will somehow overcome this problem," Brigadier Sarath Munasinghe said.
